message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Isotopes** | • ¹H (protium) – most common
• ²H (deuterium) – stable isotope, ~0.015% natural abundance
• ³H (tritium) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | | **Boiling point (STP)** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | | **Melting point (STP)** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) | | **Molar volume (ideal gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | | **Color / Odor / Taste** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless | | **State at room temperature** | Gas | | **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air | | **Diffusivity** | Highest among gases; diffuses through solids and liquids | | **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens, oxygen, nitrogen oxides, etc. | | **Common compounds** | H₂O, HCl, H₂SO₄, NH₃, CH₄, C₂H₂, etc. | | **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔH°f)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (elementary state) | | **Standard entropy (S°)** | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | | **Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (ΔG°f)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (elementary state) | ### Additional Notes * **Physical behavior** – Hydrogen is the lightest element; it rises rapidly in air and can form explosive mixtures with oxygen or air. * **Chemical behavior** – It readily forms covalent bonds (e.g., H₂O, H₂S) and ionic bonds (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). In its elemental form, H₂ is a weak reducing agent but becomes a powerful one when combined with metals (forming metal hydrides). * **Isotopic differences** – Deuterium and tritium have slightly higher boiling/melting points and lower vapor pressures due to their greater masses. Tritium’s radioactivity makes it useful in nuclear fusion research and as a tracer in biochemical studies. These values are standard at 25 °C (298 K) and 1 atm unless otherwise specified.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the different properties of Hydrogen?" They want properties of hydrogen. We can use the tool to look up major contributions of a particular scientist, but that's not relevant. There's no tool for chemical properties. So we need to answer manually. Provide properties: atomic number, mass, electronegativity, ionization energy, electron affinity, boiling point, melting point, density, etc. Also mention isotopes: H-1, H-2 (deuterium), H-3 (tritium). Physical properties: colorless, odorless, tasteless gas at STP; flammable; low density; high diffusivity; forms diatomic molecules. Chemical properties: highly reactive, forms hydrides, acids, bases, etc. Provide some key data.

We should provide a concise but thorough answer. No tool needed.
